title: Rent Hike — Recalculating
description:
A text arrived. Rent going up 50,000 won.

{name} started calculating.
50,000 won a month. 600,000 won a year. Three million won over five years.

That money doesn't just disappear.
It's money leaving the investable column every month.
Run compound interest on it and the story changes.

choices.text: Negotiate with the landlord. Protect the margin.
choices.result_text:
Negotiated the increase down.
30,000 won a month saved — 360,000 won a year.
Small differences aren't small once compound interest gets involved.

choices.text: Accept it. Cut other expenses.
choices.result_text:
Cancelled two subscriptions.
Combined: 48,000 won.
Made up for the rent increase somewhere else.

choices.text: Move to a cheaper place. Lower fixed costs.
choices.result_text:
Found a cheaper room and moved.
Moving costs: 350,000 won.
Break-even in seven months.

title: Crypto Futures Temptation
description:
1 AM. Crypto futures profit screenshots are flooding the group chat.
'200% in one hour', 'This actually works.'

Everyone who knows is already in — or so the word goes.
10x leverage, 100,000 won margin to get 1 million won exposure.
{name}'s fingers hover over the screen.
The exchange app download button is right there.

choices.text: Do not install the exchange app
choices.result_text:
You closed the download page and muted the group chat.
At 2 AM, your hand reached for the screen again, but the app was not there.

choices.text: Close the chat but leave the download page open
choices.result_text:
You closed only the group chat.
The download button remained open in the browser.

choices.text: Full leverage. All in.
choices.result_text: Everything's on the line. Which way fate swings — that won't be known until morning.

title: Breaking: Rates, Tax, Housing — All at Once
description:
10:03 AM.

Breaking news alerts fired.
Base rate held. Capital gains tax eased. Some speculation zones lifted.

Three things dropped simultaneously.
The portfolio screen flickered.

The gap between those who move now and those who wait — this is where it opens.

choices.text: Adjust risk asset weighting. Defensive reposition.
choices.result_text:
Increased bonds, reduced leverage.
Market was up 2% the next day.
Whether the defensive call was right — that'll be known in three months.

choices.text: Watch and wait for now.
choices.result_text:
Closed the screen.
Reopened it two hours later.
Market whipped around and ended up back where it started.

choices.text: Move fast into policy-benefit sectors.
choices.result_text:
Bought a real estate ETF.
Up 3.2% on the day.
Down 1.8% the next. Still in the green.

title: Election Thematic Plays
description:
Election season again. YouTube is flooded with 'sector beneficiaries by candidate' analysis.
Thumbnails reading 'This stock 3x if this candidate wins.'

A certain sector actually surged last election — it happened.
{name} felt the FOMO of maybe missing this wave.
But nobody knows who wins an election.

choices.text: Buy early, before the rumor spreads.
choices.result_text: Got in ahead of the noise. Being quick to read the room beats having the information.

choices.text: Ignore the election plays.
choices.result_text: Know the risks of speculative theme trading. Stayed out. FOMO is real — no regrets though.

choices.text: Quick in and out. Scalp trade.
choices.result_text: In and out in the blink of an eye. Fast judgment paid off this time.

choices.text: Watch the chart. Do nothing.
choices.result_text: Might have missed the move. But not losing anything is enough for today.

title: Sudden Layoff Rumors
description:
Lunch hour. A strange tension in the company chat.
'you heard there's restructuring this month' — one post.

Similar rumors are circulating on stock forums too. About a company {name} holds.
No official announcement — but the stock is already sliding toward -8%.
Believe the rumor and sell, or wait for the official word?

choices.text: Coolheadedly assess the situation first.
choices.result_text: Checked whether it's rumor or fact before anything else. Getting the facts before the feelings matters.

choices.text: Too anxious to do anything.
choices.result_text: Every worst-case scenario played out in the mind. This night is going to be long.

choices.text: Reverse the rumor — take a position.
choices.result_text: Went in bold while others panic-sold. The moment fear became opportunity.

title: Phone Smashed
description:
You dropped your phone while walking. The screen shattered.
An official repair costs 300,000 won. An independent shop quoted 180,000 won for a used screen assembly.

The expense was sudden, and it would come out of money set aside for investing.
Before paying, {name} compared the two shops' warranties and reviews.

choices.text: Leave it with the official service center
choices.result_text: You paid 300,000 won to repair the same device. The unplanned expense hurt, but the official warranty remained.

choices.text: Repair it with a used screen assembly
choices.result_text: A well-reviewed independent shop fitted a used screen assembly. It cost 180,000 won, though the colors flickered now and then.

title: Sports Betting Link in Group Chat
description:
Unknown number dropped a link in the chat.
'100% analysis for this week. If you watch Daon closely, you'd know.'

Eleven people in the room.
Someone commented 'I hit it last week.'

{name} spent three seconds debating whether to click.

choices.text: Ignore the link. Leave the group chat.
choices.result_text:
Left the chat.
Never found out how the week turned out.
Sometimes not knowing is the better deal.

choices.text: Peek at it for a second.
choices.result_text:
Clicked the link.
A sign-up form appeared.
Hit back. Just looked this time.

choices.text: Try it once. Tiny amount.
choices.result_text:
Put in 10,000 won.
Got it wrong.
Called it 10,000 won in tuition.

title: Payday — Running the Numbers
description:
Paycheck in.
Card bill out at the same moment.

Checked the balance.
How much is actually investable this month?

{name} started subtracting fixed costs one by one.
Rent, food, phone, subscriptions, card payment.
The number shrank faster than expected.

choices.text: Pay off the card in full. Invest what's left.
choices.result_text:
Got to the investable amount.
Smaller than expected.
Still bigger than zero. Decided to cut more next month.

choices.text: Minimum payment only. Put the rest into the market.
choices.result_text:
Transferred the minimum.
Moved the rest to the investment account.
Interest started accumulating. Card interest.

choices.text: Skip investing this month.
choices.result_text:
Took a break this month.
Paid off the card completely.
Balance was higher than usual. Didn't feel good.

title: Balance: -34,200 won
description:
8:41 AM.
Bank app notification.

'Your account is negative. Overdraft interest is being applied.'

The number: -34,200 won.
Overdraft limit remaining: 4.9678 million won.

{name} closed the app and reopened it.
The number was the same.

choices.text: Deposit and cover it today.
choices.result_text:
Reached out to someone.
Borrowed the money.
Deposited it that evening. The negative disappeared.

choices.text: Turn off the notifications. Let it sit.
choices.result_text:
Went into notification settings.
Turned them off.
Decided not to calculate how much the daily interest was.

choices.text: Liquidate part of the portfolio to cover it.
choices.result_text:
Sold part of a profitable position.
After tax it was just enough.
Account went to zero. Felt like starting over.

choices.text: Deepen the overdraft. Use it for investing.
choices.result_text:
Pulled to the limit.
Transferred to the investment account.
Recalculated interest rate vs. expected return. Razor thin.

title: Jeonse Fraud News — Real Estate Sector Falls
description:
300 jeonse fraud victims in the news.

Real estate stocks were dropping from the opening bell.
Construction -3.2%. REITs -4.1%. Real estate platforms -2.8%.

{name} looked at the portfolio.
When fear makes the price — is this the opportunity, or is the bottom still ahead?

choices.text: More downside likely — wait and watch.
choices.result_text:
Kept hands off.
Next day brought more selling.
Rebound started on day three. The wait was right.

choices.text: Start staged buying into the panic sell zone.
choices.result_text:
Bought a third.
Down another 2% the next day.
Bought another third. That's why you stage it.

choices.text: Sell the existing position. Cut losses.
choices.result_text:
Stopped out.
-6.3%.
Painful number — but it fell further. Called this one right.

title: Youth Subsidy Controversy
description:
Youth subsidy policy announced. Cash payment if certain conditions are met.
Social media split on it.

If the subsidy actually gets distributed, consumer sentiment could tick up.
Domestic demand stocks started moving.
{name} considered riding the wave — or watching from the sidelines.

choices.text: Check eligibility carefully and apply.
choices.result_text: Reviewed the eligibility and procedures thoroughly and submitted the application. Not embarrassing — it's a right.

choices.text: Get sucked into the online debate.
choices.result_text: Started an argument online. Burned all the energy. Got nothing in return.

choices.text: Put the subsidy to work as seed money.
choices.result_text: Deposited the cash straight into the investment account. Even handouts compound when you invest them.

choices.text: Ignore the whole thing.
choices.result_text: Figured it had nothing to do with {name} anyway. Indifference was the easiest choice.

title: "One Shot Is All It Takes"
description:
A senior at work said it over drinks. 'I made 100 million won on crypto last year. You just need the right timing.'
{name} couldn't shake it even back home.

Checked the balance in the banking app. What if all of it went in right now?
Rationality says no. Emotion whispers maybe.
{name} has to make an important decision tonight.

choices.text: Hear it — then coldly run the numbers.
choices.result_text: Calculated the actual odds of a one-shot win. Numbers don't lie.

choices.text: Get shaken. Start comparing to others.
choices.result_text: Got swept up in other people's success stories. Comparing is the most dangerous investment psychology.

choices.text: Put everything on one bet.
choices.result_text: Believed in the one shot. Whatever happens — this choice will be remembered for a long time.

choices.text: Cover your ears and leave.
choices.result_text: Chose not to listen. Walking away from temptation takes courage too.

title: ETF Screenshot
description:
A 20-year US Large-Cap ETF return chart was posted to the finance community.
600% over 20 years. Hundreds of comments.

'Should've started earlier.' {name}'s hands are still empty.
Looking at the screenshot triggered an urge to start something, now.
Start diversified investing immediately — or study more first?

choices.text: Analyze the ETF's underlying holdings properly.
choices.result_text: While others posted screenshots, looked at the substance. The risk behind a trend has to be examined.

choices.text: Follow the crowd. Buy a small amount.
choices.result_text: Triggered by the screenshot, hit the buy button just like everyone else. Herd psychology is hard to resist.

choices.text: Turn the screenshot trend into content for the channel.
choices.result_text: Made the flow itself into content rather than riding it. Reading the times opened a different door.

title: Housing Regulation Rumor
description:
Real estate forums are buzzing. 'Stricter lending regulations confirmed next month' — source unknown.
Already hit 100,000 views.

Some people are moving before the official announcement.
{name} holds assets partially in real estate.
Act on the rumor, or wait for the official word?

choices.text: Move preemptively before the official announcement.
choices.result_text: Adjusted position before the rumor became fact. Speed of information is profit.

choices.text: Let panic override logic. Sell emotionally.
choices.result_text: Fear moved the finger before the brain did. Sold in a rush.

choices.text: Reverse the rumor — wait for the dip and buy.
choices.result_text: Bought when everyone was selling. Fear is often just another name for opportunity.

title: Portfolio Rebalancing Dilemma
description: Opened the investment app and stopped. One position is glowing blue alone, now over 60% of the whole portfolio. The gains are sweet — but leaving it there means one swing could take everything down. {name} stared at the screen, finger frozen in the air.

choices.text: Rebalance now — take some profit and spread safely.
choices.result_text: Trimmed the oversized position and rebalanced. Protecting gains is also part of investing.

choices.text: Hold longer — this could be the start of a bull run.
choices.result_text: Decided to ride it between greed and conviction. Sleepless nights ahead — but that's the investor's burden.

choices.text: Watch a few expert YouTube videos first.
choices.result_text: Closed three hours of videos with no conclusion — but at least understood the principles of rebalancing. Knowledge speeds up future decisions.

title: Stock Tip in the Group Chat
description: 2 PM. A message in the stock group chat: 'Timing to enter now — sharp rise expected tomorrow.' Sender is a someone who called it right once before. Over 100 people in the room and already half are typing 'you're buying.' Whether this is real or noise — the palm holding the phone is sweating.

choices.text: Small bet — tuition if wrong.
choices.result_text: Bought 100,000 won worth. Next day the stock quietly dropped — and the group chat went silent.

choices.text: Ignore it. Close the app.
choices.result_text: Muted the group chat. Confirmed once again: good information doesn't come to group chats first.

choices.text: Verify the source directly.
choices.result_text: Searched the disclosures. No basis whatsoever. The fact-checking habit protected the wallet again.

title: Market Crash Alert
description: 3:17 AM. Phone went off. US market -4.8%. NASDAQ circuit breaker triggered. Breaking news everywhere. Korean market opens at 9. 5 hours and 45 minutes to make a decision. {name} kicked off the covers, got up, and opened the laptop.

choices.text: Full liquidation the moment the market opens.
choices.result_text: At 9:00 sharp, the execution screen went red. Locking in a loss mixed strangely with the relief of not losing more.

choices.text: Hold. Long-term investors don't trade the night.
choices.result_text: Closed the screen and forced eyes shut. A week later the market was halfway recovered — and {name}'s nerves were harder.

choices.text: Buy more. Fear is the opportunity.
choices.result_text: Put in staged buys while panic selling flooded the market. Could have been wrong — but this choice might become legend later.

title: Dividend Deposit
description: A KakaoBank notification arrived at lunch. '47,200 won dividend deposited.' Money from a stock held without much expectation. Small — but the sensation of money arriving without doing anything is entirely new. Took a screenshot of the deposit notification and stared at it for a while.

choices.text: Reinvest the dividend immediately.
choices.result_text: Put the money right back into the same stock. The magic of compounding starts with exactly this small action.

choices.text: Spend it on a nice dinner. Small joy.
choices.result_text: Used the dividend money for samgyeopsal. Meat paid for by the market always tastes different.

title: The Stop-Loss Decision
description: A stock bought confidently two weeks ago is down -25%. First it was 'it'll recover if I wait.' But today closed down again. Where to draw the stop-loss line — {name} stared at the red number and the hand stopped. A voice in the back of the mind kept saying 'selling now means failure.'

choices.text: Stop-loss now — before it gets worse.
choices.result_text: Fingers trembled — but hit the sell button. Accepting a loss is painful, but it's how you grow as an investor.

choices.text: Average down — lower the cost basis.
choices.result_text: Added more to bring the average price down. Could turn out right — could fall further. For now, the only option is to wait.

choices.text: Just leave it. Nobody knows anyway.
choices.result_text: Wanted to delete the app. Closed it instead. Closing your eyes doesn't make the loss disappear.

title: IPO Subscription
description: A subscription opened for a hot K-beauty startup IPO. SNS is buzzing with 'guaranteed double on listing day.' Competition ratio already past 820:1, and the brokerage app is sluggish under load. {name} has 500,000 won in subscription deposit ready and is hesitating over the click.

choices.text: Apply — leave it to luck.
choices.result_text: Results in three weeks. Only allocated two shares — but the stock nudged up on listing day for a modest gain.

choices.text: Pass — the hype is already priced in.
choices.result_text: Judged that 820:1 hype was already fully reflected in the price. Cold-eyed analysis protected the wallet.

title: Starting to Learn ETFs
description: 11 PM. The YouTube algorithm recommended 'The Complete US Large-Cap ETF Investing Method.' Clicked out of curiosity and watched three videos back to back. The concept of investing in the whole market without the stress of picking individual stocks sounded appealing. {name} put down the beer and pulled out a notepad.

choices.text: Start studying ETFs seriously right now.
choices.result_text: Spent a week digging into ETF structure, expense ratios, and currency exposure. The more it made sense, the less the fear.

choices.text: Stick to what's already known — comfort matters.
choices.result_text: Closed the video and opened the usual watchlist. Familiar comfort felt better tonight.

title: Real Estate Bubble Fear
description: Three economists appeared on the evening news simultaneously warning that 'the real estate bubble collapse is imminent.' The comment section is split 50/50 between 'this is real this time' and 'they're always wrong.' {name}'s portfolio holds a fair amount of real estate REITs. Anxiously nursing a coffee, refreshing the return screen over and over.

choices.text: Reduce real estate exposure. Safety first.
choices.result_text: Sold some REITs and raised cash. Whether the bubble bursts or not — the peace of mind came first.

choices.text: Buy more. Fear marks the bottom.
choices.result_text: Took the news warning as a contrarian signal and added to the position. Could be wrong — but this is the path {name} chose.

choices.text: Watch and wait. Gather more information.
choices.result_text: Decided not to move hastily. Reminded {name}self that doing nothing in uncertainty is also a strategy.

title: Recession Fears
description: 10 AM, Ministry of Finance announcement. GDP growth forecast slashed from 2.1% to 0.9%. KOSPI dropped nearly 2% immediately after. Exchange rate charging toward 1,400 won, brokerage research reports overflowing with the words 'possible recession entry.' {name} forgot about lunch and stared at the screen.

choices.text: Rotate into defensive assets.
choices.result_text: Trimmed growth stocks and restructured into bonds and dividend plays. Those who prepare when the market fears are the ones who survive.

choices.text: Recession is opportunity — contrarian buy.
choices.result_text: Chose to buy while everyone sold. History has often sided with those who buy into fear.

title: Reading the Investment Bible
description: Saturday morning, picked up a Buffett biography at the bookstore. Got home, made a coffee, sat on the sofa. Couldn't look away from it all weekend. The story of an investor returning to first principles through the noise of the market quietly steadied {name}'s wavering mind.

choices.text: Commit to becoming a principles-based investor.
choices.result_text: Turned off about half the app notifications. Started opening annual reports instead of the daily chart. For the first time, investing felt enjoyable.

choices.text: Theory and reality are different. Reading it is enough.
choices.result_text: Understood Buffett's principles — but concluded the distance from {name}'s reality was still large. The mental frame shifted a little though.

title: Senior's Inside Information
description: After-work dinner. A senior in the same department leaned over with a glass. 'This company — next month's earnings are going to be huge. Supply contract just closed. Just between us.' The senior's eyes were serious. Trading on inside information is illegal — but {name}'s hand was already moving toward the stock app.

choices.text: Trust it and buy. Can't miss this.
choices.result_text: Stock was up 20% after the earnings release next month. Made money — but hands kept shaking. Couldn't tell anyone about this.

choices.text: Politely decline. Pretend not to have heard.
choices.result_text: Quietly told the senior 'you'd rather not hear that kind of thing.' The senior laughed it off awkwardly — and {name}'s conscience slept easily that night.

choices.text: Research it independently. Do it legally.
choices.result_text: Took only the hint and dug into the disclosures and news independently. Found sufficient grounds from public information alone. Made the call the clean way.

title: Financial Income Tax
description: Tax season arrived. Opened the tax authority site — too many unfamiliar categories. Asked a friend who said 'if dividend and interest income exceeds 20 million won, it becomes comprehensive taxation.' {name} calculated last year's financial income — hovering right around that threshold. Misreporting taxes now could create much bigger problems later.

choices.text: Consult a tax accountant.
choices.result_text: Consultation fee of 200,000 won — but came away with a tax optimization strategy too. Expert advice always earns its fee.

choices.text: Study it personally. Tax is investing too.
choices.result_text: Dug through the National Tax Service YouTube and blogs and filed the return manually. Painful — but taxes don't feel scary anymore.

title: DCA Commitment
description: Auto-transfer scheduled for the day after payday. 300,000 won monthly, US Large-Cap ETF. Finally decided to believe that consistency matters more than returns. {name} screenshotted the settings screen and made a quiet promise — this time, no cancelling halfway through.

choices.text: Set the auto-transfer and forget about it.
choices.result_text: Checked it six months later — returns were ordinary, but the balance had been building steadily. Consistency never betrays.

choices.text: Wait for the right timing. Not yet.
choices.result_text: Waited for the perfect timing. Three months passed. That timing never came.

title: Crypto Mania
description: The whole social feed is crypto. High school classmate posted a KakaoTalk status about making 30 million won on Corecoin. A junior at work talks about nothing but coins at lunch. Am you the only one who doesn't know? Am you falling behind? {name} downloaded the Upbit app for the first time.

choices.text: Get in a little — quiet the FOMO.
choices.result_text:
Put in 500,000 won. First it doubled.
Then halved. Crept back up to -30%.
Should sell — hand wouldn't move.
That was the pull of crypto. The stop-loss becomes impossible.

choices.text: Watch. Every mania has an ending.
choices.result_text:
Two months later, when the crypto market fell 42%, the classmate's KakaoTalk status went quiet.
{name} said nothing.
Sometimes the best investment is not investing.

choices.text: Cut the FOMO and actually study it.
choices.result_text:
Read a blockchain whitepaper. The technology was interesting.
A principle emerged: don't put money into what {name} doesn't understand.
That one principle would end up saving {name} more than once.

title: First Overseas Stock
description: Bought Orca stock for the first time. Paying in dollars, waking up at 3 AM for US market close, and having to self-report capital gains tax above 2.5 million won — {name} found all of this out today. More complex than expected. {name} sat with the currency converter open, staring blankly.

choices.text: Study all of it — exchange rate, taxes, time zones.
choices.result_text: Spent a month digging into everything about overseas investing. Complex — but now the global market feels like home turf.

choices.text: Small amount first. Learn by doing.
choices.result_text: Didn't fully understand — but got a foot in the water. A $100 experience will protect $1,000 later.

choices.text: Too complicated. Stick to domestic stocks.
choices.result_text: Decided to get good at the market already understood. Investing within your knowledge boundary is also strategy.

title: Annual Return Check
description: January 1st. Opened the 'annual return report' in the brokerage app. +7.3%. KOSPI benchmark: +11.2%. A year of hard work — and the number on the screen says the market was beaten by less than average. Good enough or not? What to change? Is it fine? No one gives the answer.

choices.text: Analyze the data and revise the strategy.
choices.result_text: Went through what dragged the numbers down and what calls were right. Turning failure into data is real skill.

choices.text: Good job — celebrate surviving without losing.
choices.result_text: Even below market average — protecting principal while lasting a full year is already something remarkable. Tomorrow's {name} is stronger than today's.

choices.text: Disappointed. Start over from scratch.
choices.result_text: Decided to clear everything and rebuild from basics. No shame in it — a late awakening beats a fast surrender.

title: Discovering DCA Investing
description:
Learned something watching YouTube.
'Just putting a fixed amount into an ETF every month generates long-term gains.'

No complex stock analysis needed. No timing required.
Just set up an auto-transfer and put money in every month.

Simple. Which somehow made it harder to believe.

choices.text: Start DCA investing in ETFs right away.
choices.result_text:
Set the auto-transfer. The same amount flows into the market every month.
Boring. That's the strategy.
Given enough time, the market does the work.

choices.text: Study more before deciding.
choices.result_text:
The studying stretched on. But the more {name} learned, the more interesting it got.
Knowledge doesn't incur losses.
Slowly starting to understand why those who invest with comprehension last longer.

choices.text: Individual stocks are more interesting than ETFs.
choices.result_text:
Picked a stock. If it goes up, credit the insight. If it falls, blame the market.
Fun. And risky.
Both statements were true.

title: First Dividend
description:
Dividend payment day.

A text arrived in the morning.
'43,200 won dividend deposited.'

Money arrived without working.
43,200 won. A small amount.
But understanding this mechanism for the first time — something shifted.

choices.text: Reinvest the dividend. Compound it.
choices.result_text: The dividend was reinvested. A small snowball started rolling.

choices.text: Eat something good with this today.
choices.result_text: The first reward from making money work. Small — but different.

title: Real Estate Regulation Announcement
description:
The government announced additional real estate regulations.

Reduced loan limits, higher acquisition tax, gap investment restrictions...

Anyone considering a purchase went back to the calculator.
Predictions came out that demand for lease would increase, pushing up lease prices.

Every announcement has market consequences.

choices.text: Study investment vehicles that get around the regulation.
choices.result_text: Where regulations appear, gaps appear. The educated find them first.

choices.text: Move safely into bonds or deposits.
choices.result_text: Reduced risk. Returns shrank too — but sleep came easily.

choices.text: Stay put. Don't trust government announcements.
choices.result_text: Time will tell.

title: Fear & Greed Index: 100
description:
A red alert appeared on the market analysis section of the investment app.

'Fear & Greed Index: 98 — Extreme Greed'

They say you should sell when everyone wants to buy.
But if you don't buy now, maybe it goes higher.

The hardest thing in investing isn't numbers — it's emotions.

choices.text: Guard against greed. Realize some gains.
choices.result_text: Market corrected a few days later. Beating greed turned into profit.

choices.text: Ride the momentum. Buy more.
choices.result_text: Timing was poor. Bought near the top.

choices.text: Do nothing. Stick to the plan.
choices.result_text: Kept to the principle. Patience is the long-term investor's sharpest weapon.

title: Portfolio Check
description:
End of quarter. Opened the investment app.

The original allocation was broken.
One position had surged and now held 60% of the total.

Leaving it this way means leaning too heavily on one side.
Rebalance — or load more onto what's working?

choices.text: Rebalance back to the original allocation.
choices.result_text: Realized some gains and filled out the other assets. Principles bring comfort.

choices.text: Keep holding the winner.
choices.result_text: Went higher. Of course — it would also fall harder when it falls. Already knew that.

title: Trust as an Asset
description:
Walking the straight road has apparently been accumulating somewhere.
Someone from a brief past crossing has reached out.
"In times like these, people who keep their principles are rare.
May I ask you something?"
Reputation builds slowly — and then one day, it just works.

choices.text: Meet them gladly. Connections are assets too.
choices.result_text:
A verified person introduced a verified route.
Not flashy, but safe and legal opportunity.
Walking straight means these are the connections that accumulate.
Confirmed again: not losing is also winning.

choices.text: Too busy right now. Decline.
choices.result_text:
Turned it down. They weren't offended.
Someone who's walked the straight road earns that kind of latitude.
Opportunity comes again. For people with principles it does.

title: The Institutional Door Opens
description:
The path walked so far has opened a particular door.
Private Banking center of a securities firm. A place ordinary clients don't enter.

"We can share our research team's reports in advance.
Within legal bounds, of course — but earlier information is better."

Not the same starting line. A door that only opens for those who walked the straight road.

choices.text: Accept PB services.
choices.result_text:
Now receiving analysis one day ahead of the market.
Public information — but the interpretation is different.
Swimming in the same pool — just a different lane. Didn't know that until now.

choices.text: Thank you — but want to decide independently.
choices.result_text:
Chose to trust {name}'s own judgment.
The contact was disappointed but understanding.
"Call if you change your mind."
That card stayed in the wallet.

title: Gray Zone Information
description:
Late night pojangmacha. A middle-aged man strikes up a conversation.

"...Hold on. I know your type. Someone who doesn't just take the orthodox route."

True. How did he know?
He lowers his voice.
"Certain materials stocks will move this month.
Not internal — just a strong gut feeling."

Legally fine — probably.

choices.text: Act on the information. Take a position.
choices.result_text:
Got into position. Right or wrong — unclear.
If the man is right: profit. If not: loss.
But this kind of information only comes to those who know how to find it.

choices.text: Ignore it. Rumors are rumors.
choices.result_text:
Just drank. Good soju.
The market is overflowing with noise that calls itself information.
Knowing what to discard is also a skill.

choices.text: Find out more about this person.
choices.result_text:
Tracked him down a few days later. Quite an interesting figure.
Said he doesn't sell information. Then why did he say it?
{name} wanted to understand the reason.

title: The Underground Network
description:
At some point, a different kind of person started reaching out.
Outside the institutional system — but holding extraordinary information.

"You're not the type to follow the rules.
I don't mind that. Come check out our circle."

A Telegram channel link.
Clicked it. A world of different dimensions.

choices.text: Join the network.
choices.result_text:
The quality of information was different. Moves were different.
Teetering on the edge of the legal boundary.
Returns went up. Conscience went down a little.
A life of both moving simultaneously had begun.

choices.text: Won't go any deeper than this.
choices.result_text:
Closed the link. This far and no further.
Already crossed several lines — but not this one.
{name} still had one last line left.

title: IPO Jackpot Forecast
description:
Word came from a senior at work.
"This AI semiconductor IPO — institutions are pushing it hard.
Equality allocation subscribers should expect two or three upper-limit days as a baseline."

Deposit gets locked up and allocation is luck —
but in this market, there's a feeling it'll come through.
How much to put in is the only question.

choices.text: Go big — when else?
choices.result_text:
Applied for the subscription. The days with capital frozen feel long.
Find out on listing day.
{name} waited, watching numbers dance on the screen.

choices.text: Small amount only — diversification is principle.
choices.result_text:
Put in a portion. Let go of the greed.
An amount that can be absorbed if lost — profit if won, experience if not.
This is the mindset that keeps an investor going long.

choices.text: IPOs are gambling — pass.
choices.result_text:
IPOs are ultimately a timing game.
If not convinced, better not to enter.
{name} closed the screen. Waiting for the next opportunity.

title: Redevelopment Zone Information
description:
A contact from long ago reached out.
"Minjun, this is just between us. I heard from someone at the district office —
that whole villa neighborhood is confirmed for redevelopment zone designation next year.
There's a property listed at 30% of market price, quietly selling hand to hand."

The value of real estate information is all in the timing.
If redevelopment confirms, multiples. If it falls through — just a run-down villa.
At this price, it's all-in. The judgment is yours.

choices.text: Go all in — this could be the last shot at Gangnam.
choices.result_text:
Signed the contract.
Standing in front of the worn-down villa with the key in hand,
{name} was briefly confused about whether this was a dream or reality.
The waiting begins. Waiting for the official redevelopment confirmation notice.

choices.text: Put in a portion — spread the risk.
choices.result_text:
Judged that all-in was too much.
Invested part and kept the rest as cash.
"Half is better than losing everything chasing greed."
{name} self-convinced.

choices.text: Inside information is dangerous. Decline.
choices.result_text:
Trading on insider information carries legal risk.
Tempting — but passing.
{name} hung up and looked out the window.
Clean hands, that was the choice.

title: Pre-Completion Redevelopment Buyout
description:
The redevelopment plan finally cleared its management approval. Before the apartment complex replaces the old villas, the developer offered to buy the members' stakes in one sweep.

The offer: 2.6 billion won.

It was a number you could not have imagined when you first stamped the contract. Sell now and the long wait ends here. Hold on and the occupancy right may be worth more, but more assessments and more years will follow.

choices.text: Sell the stake — cash out 2.6 billion won
choices.result_text: You signed the sale agreement. The key to an old villa became 2.6 billion won. It was not one lucky hit. It was the distress sale, the association meetings, and the months of waiting whenever the project stalled.

choices.text: Keep the occupancy right — it is not time to sell
choices.result_text: You declined. Instead of a number in the bank, you kept the occupancy right. Beyond the construction fence, you looked at a home that did not exist yet. No one knew whether it meant a larger return or only a longer wait.

title: Sangchul's Tip — A Distress Sale
description:
Pushed open the real estate office door. Sangchul waved {name} over.

"Minjun, this isn't something I tell just anyone."

Station-adjacent commercial building share, distress sale. Owner needs cash fast — listed way below market.

"In 30 years of looking, this is one I can count on my fingers. But money — nothing's certain. Know that before you go in."

Information only a trusted person hears. The decision is still yours to make.

choices.text: Trust Sangchul's eye. Go in big.
choices.result_text:
Signed the contract.
Sangchul clapped a shoulder. "Now the job is waiting."

choices.text: Try a small amount.
choices.result_text:
"Betting small is also a skill." Sangchul smiled.
Only as much as {name} could absorb without crumbling.

choices.text: Thanks — sitting this one out.
choices.result_text:
"Right. Not going in is also a judgment call."
Sangchul didn't take it personally. That's what makes him different.

title: Sangchul's Warning — The Market Is Off
description:
Gukbap place. Sangchul set down his spoon and spoke.

"Have you been watching the market lately? Everyone's too excited. I've seen this atmosphere three times in 30 years — all three times it ended badly."

"Selling when it's up is the hardest thing. Because of greed. But the ones who manage to do it — those are the ones who survive."

The portfolio flickered through {name}'s mind.

choices.text: Take the advice. Review the risk exposure.
choices.result_text:
Went back through the portfolio that night.
Saw the places too heavily loaded.
An old man's words are 30 years of tuition, given for free.

choices.text: "This time is different" — go with my own judgment.
choices.result_text:
"That line — I heard it before each of those three crashes."
Sangchul didn't push further. "It's your money."

title: Money grew for the first time
description:
You looked at your phone screen.
The number had changed.

The ETF you bought yesterday was up 3.2%.
In won, that was 48,000.

Nothing huge. And yet your hands were shaking.
While you did nothing at all, money had made money.

choices.text: I should buy more — this is the right direction
choices.result_text:
It was a small amount, but it gave you conviction.
Little by little, steadily, like this.

choices.text: Sell now and lock it in — it's only mine once it's in hand
choices.result_text:
You locked in the 48,000 won.
And immediately regretted it. That afternoon it climbed another 2%.

title: Money shrank for the first time
description:
You opened the app before bed.

Red numbers.

-7.4%. In a single day, 7.4% of your investment was gone.

Reason says, 'Long-term investing, hold the line.'
Instinct screams, 'Sell, right now.'

choices.text: I held — this is a long game
choices.result_text:
You held on.
The next month it recovered 6%. Rising slower than it falls is the reality of investing.

choices.text: I sold — before losing more
choices.result_text:
You sold. Your mind felt at ease.
And three weeks later, that stock was right back where it started.

title: The Temptation of Leverage
description:
The YouTube algorithm served it up.
'3x Leveraged ETF, 280% Return in One Year'

The comments were ecstatic; several wrote 'I did it too.'

{name} pulled out the calculator.
Multiply what you have now by three.

choices.text: Just a portion in leverage — 30% should be fine
choices.result_text:
You put 30% into a 3x leveraged fund.
That was effectively betting 90% of the whole portfolio on one direction.

choices.text: Skip it — the comments never mention the losses
choices.result_text:
You closed the video.
The title said '280%,' but the share of people who lost over the same period was nowhere on screen.

title: The Crash
description:
The market was collapsing.

Shock from U.S. jobs data. Circuit breakers triggered. KOSPI -8%.

Social media was flooded with 'I sold everything' and 'It's already too late.'
{name}'s portfolio was a wall of bright red numbers too.

choices.text: Use the fear — a chance to buy in tranches
choices.result_text:
You were able to buy into the fear.
Two months later the market rebounded 50%, and that position doubled.

choices.text: Sell everything — I have to protect the principal
choices.result_text:
You sold. You locked in the loss.
After that you didn't look at the market for a while.

choices.text: Do nothing — I won't be shaken
choices.result_text:
You held. That was all.
That was the first time you learned that holding, too, is a strategy.

title: Dividend Deposited
description:
A text notification came in.

'Dividend deposited: 234,000 won'

It was the first time.
You'd done nothing, and money landed in your account.

So this is passive income.

choices.text: Reinvest it — the start of compounding
choices.result_text:
You put the 234,000 won back into the market.
A small snowball had started to roll.

choices.text: Spend it on living costs — things are tight right now
choices.result_text:
You treated yourself to something good with the 234,000 won.
This month was a little less tight.

title: An Investing Night in the Goshiwon
description:
2 a.m.

In a two-pyeong goshiwon room, you turned on the laptop.

It was the hour the U.S. Market opened.
Upstairs, someone snoring.
Next door, the clatter of a keyboard.

{name} watched the order book.

choices.text: Don't trade tonight — emotional decisions are poison
choices.result_text:
You closed the laptop.
Decisions made on late-night emotion always ended in regret.

choices.text: Buy — I can't face morning while it's still down
choices.result_text:
You bought. And fell asleep at 4 a.m.
The next day, -3%. Exhaustion and losses piled up together.

title: Housing Price News
description:
You turned on the news.

'Gangnam apartments break 2.5 billion won on average'

2.5 billion.
You couldn't even calculate how many times {name}'s account balance that was.

But how did the people living in those apartments manage to buy them?

choices.text: Start studying real estate
choices.result_text:
Leverage, jeonse, gap investing.
You started memorizing the words.

choices.text: Turn off the TV — that number has nothing to do with my reality
choices.result_text:
You turned it off.
Whether Gangnam prices rose or not, today's work still had to be done today.
